assessment.nobel_worthiness: Practical correction of spherical aberration in electron lenses opened the door to routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy of atoms, interfaces and defects in transmission and scanning transmission electron microscopy. It is a genuine invention that made visible what could not be seen before, and it underpins much of modern materials, nanoscience and quantum-device characterisation.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the optical theory of correctors, Haider led the first working TEM corrector, and Krivanek built the STEM corrector; this three-person split follows the original-work principle well. Other contributors (for example Urban, Zach, Dellby) are not in the supplied credit, and the allocation between TEM and STEM routes is a point the committee would want to check carefully against the historical record.
assessment.maturity: Aberration-corrected instruments have been commercial and ubiquitous for about two decades, with abundant independent confirmation. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature, though electron microscopy was recently honoured in the Chemistry prize (cryo-EM), which may bear on how the physics side frames it.
uncertainties: Whether the field would be seen as physics rather than chemistry or instrumentation in the committee's framing, given the recent cryo-EM prize.
Possible additional deserving contributors beyond the three supplied names; priority between TEM and STEM correctors.
I am recalling the history from memory and have not verified individual priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised the Mott-insulator transition and Hubbard-type models in a clean, tunable setting, creating a new platform for quantum simulation of correlated matter. This is a new tool that opens a door to phenomena inaccessible in real solids, and it has produced many verified experiments.
assessment.attribution: The decisive experimental demonstrations are credited to Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger (bosonic Mott insulator, fermionic Mott and related work); Cirac and Zoller are principally theory and proposal, and the Jaksch et al. proposal that underlies the Mott experiment is not among the credited names. Choosing the experimental three follows the original-experiment criterion but leaves theory credit unresolved.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of independent confirmation across many groups, with quantum-gas microscopes and large-scale simulations. Clearly mature, although the strongest scientific payoff (solving open correlated-matter questions) is still developing.
uncertainties: Fair split between the experimental and theoretical founders, and between the Munich/Zurich/Harvard groups and earlier Bose-Einstein condensation work already honoured.
Overlap with other AMO candidates on the longlist that credit Cirac and Zoller.
Priority details recalled from memory rather than verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator by Kane and Mele, followed by the experimental observation of edge-state transport in HgTe quantum wells by Molenkamp's group, defined a major new class of matter. The combination of theory and a decisive original experiment fits the discovery criterion well.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele are the clear theoretical originators of the Z2 classification; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental demonstration (2007) following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, whose authors are not in the credited names. This is a real attribution tension. Three-way credit is plausible but fragile.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed through ARPES and transport on multiple materials across nearly two decades; the framework is stable and broadly used. Timing is reasonable, though Haldane's earlier topological prize in 2016 overlaps conceptually.
uncertainties: Omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and of the three-dimensional topological insulator work, from the supplied credit.
Whether the committee regards this as sufficiently distinct from the 2016 prize.
Fine historical priority details recalled from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum matter, a very active new field with a clean combination of prediction and experiment.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key 2011 prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the original experimental observation (with the first author of that paper a student). Pablo Jarillo-Herrero, MacDonald and Bistritzer are a natural three, though other theorists and the collaborators who fabricated the device are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Observation has been reproduced by many groups and extended to other moire systems within a few years. Fast but real confirmation; the interpretation of the correlated phases is still debated, so the prize might be considered somewhat early.
uncertainties: Stability of the theoretical interpretation of the superconducting and correlated phases.
Whether credit should include other experimental groups or additional theorists beyond the supplied names.
Possible prematurity relative to older candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock proposed by Katori and brought to 10^-18 level precision by Ye's group is an invention that redefines precision measurement, with applications to fundamental-constant tests, geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second. Experimental, measurable and clear in significance.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the lattice-clock concept and early demonstrations; Ye drove the record accuracy and stability. The two-person split seems fair, though other groups (for example single-ion clocks and the optical frequency comb, already honoured) are adjacent and the Hall/Hansch comb prize is a necessary foundation.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by several independent labs worldwide. Recognition could be timely, particularly if the redefinition of the second proceeds, but the maturity of the broader application story is still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap with ion-clock work and the 2012 and 2005 precision-measurement prizes.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for the second's redefinition.
Details of priority recalled from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hosono's 2008 report of superconductivity in fluorine-doped LaFeAsO opened a second family of high-temperature superconductors, and subsequent rapid raising of the critical temperature to about 55 K showed it was not a one-off. This is an original experimental discovery that reshaped the study of unconventional superconductivity.
assessment.attribution: Hosono made the original discovery; Zhao's group (with Chen and others) pushed rare-earth substituted compounds to the highest Tc. Chen is also credited in the list, but the three-person split is less clean than a Hosono-plus-one configuration because the Tc advances were achieved extremely quickly by several Chinese groups.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed and replicated within months, but the pairing mechanism remains unresolved and applications limited. The discovery is solid; the interpretation is not yet stable, which may argue for waiting.
uncertainties: Fair allocation between the original discoverer and the groups that raised Tc.
The absence of an accepted mechanism and limited technological impact so far.
Details recalled from memory, not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental observation of the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological insulator films, following a concrete theoretical proposal, realised dissipationless chiral edge transport without an external magnetic field. It is a clean, verified original experiment with metrological and device interest.
assessment.attribution: Xue's group made the 2013 experimental observation; Dai, Fang and coauthors proposed the Cr/Bi-doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 route. Haldane's earlier concept and other theorists (for example Qi, Zhang, Yu) are not in the supplied credit and could complicate a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by independent groups (including at higher precision), though the effect still requires very low temperatures. Reasonably mature but less obviously transformative than the broader topological insulator discovery.
uncertainties: Credit overlap with the topological insulator and Haldane prizes, and with theorists omitted from the credited names.
Practical impact still limited by operating temperature.
Details recalled from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a Higgs-like boson at the LHC in 2012 is a landmark discovery, verifying the last missing piece of the Standard Model and an outstanding experimental achievement that clearly meets the criterion of an experimentally verified result of fundamental importance.
assessment.attribution: The discovery was made by two independent collaborations of thousands. The supplied names are leaders and spokespersons or founders rather than demonstrably the individuals who made the decisive measurements, and the committee's three-person limit makes a fair configuration difficult. Selecting three names here is a pragmatic choice, not a clear resolution of credit.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with independently confirmed properties and the theory prize awarded in 2013. Recognition of the experimental side is overdue, but the credit problem has historically blocked it.
uncertainties: Unresolved attribution among collaboration leaders versus the many who made the key analyses and detector contributions.
Whether any three-name configuration, or an organisational recognition, is acceptable under the statutes.
Details of roles recalled from memory.
